turns.request: We are Hayk (31) and Mane (29) Sargsyan and we just bought this top-floor flat in Orion. Hayk is a sommelier and runs a small wine bar in Kond; Mane is a ceramicist who sells her work online and teaches wheel classes on weekends. We love the room in the picture I attached: the terracotta wall, the soft cream sofa, the walnut sideboard, the travertine table, the olive tree and the big abstract canvas. Please make our living room feel like that, and carry the same warm palette through the rest of the flat without copying it everywhere. The long living room with the kitchen must seat 8 for Friday wine tastings: a solid dining table, comfortable chairs, a place to display bottles and glasses (a bar cabinet or open shelves), and a sofa corner for after dinner with a record player. Bedroom 1 (the big one with the ensuite) is ours: a king bed, a walk-in feel with wardrobes, two nightstands, a reading chair, and linen curtains. Bedroom 2 is Mane's studio office: a big worktable for packing orders, a desk for her laptop, open shelves to photograph and store finished pieces, good light, no carpet (clay dust). Bedroom 3 is the guest room for Hayk's parents, who fly in from Glendale for two months every summer: a queen bed, a wardrobe, a small desk and a comfortable armchair for his father, who has a bad back. The hall needs shoe storage and a mirror, and the little balcony two stools and plants. We dislike cold greys, chrome and heavy, dark bedrooms. Budget: 9,000,000 AMD for furniture.

record.message: I’ll first check the room sizes and circulation, then build a warm, cohesive scheme around your wine tastings, ceramics work and summer guests.
The flat fits the brief: two proper bedrooms, a separate ceramics office, and enough living space for an eight-seat dining area beside a lounge.

Each room is now being developed around the shared palette.

requests: We are Hayk (31) and Mane (29) Sargsyan and we just bought this top-floor flat in Orion. Hayk is a sommelier and runs a small wine bar in Kond; Mane is a ceramicist who sells her work online and teaches wheel classes on weekends. We love the room in the picture I attached: the terracotta wall, the soft cream sofa, the walnut sideboard, the travertine table, the olive tree and the big abstract canvas. Please make our living room feel like that, and carry the same warm palette through the rest of the flat without copying it everywhere. The long living room with the kitchen must seat 8 for Friday wine tastings: a solid dining table, comfortable chairs, a place to display bottles and glasses (a bar cabinet or open shelves), and a sofa corner for after dinner with a record player. Bedroom 1 (the big one with the ensuite) is ours: a king bed, a walk-in feel with wardrobes, two nightstands, a reading chair, and linen curtains. Bedroom 2 is Mane's studio office: a big worktable for packing orders, a desk for her laptop, open shelves to photograph and store finished pieces, good light, no carpet (clay dust). Bedroom 3 is the guest room for Hayk's parents, who fly in from Glendale for two months every summer: a queen bed, a wardrobe, a small desk and a comfortable armchair for his father, who has a bad back. The hall needs shoe storage and a mirror, and the little balcony two stools and plants. We dislike cold greys, chrome and heavy, dark bedrooms. Budget: 9,000,000 AMD for furniture.
